chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharjah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who seeks Allah's choice (istikhara) and is content with what Allah has done for him, Allah will choose for him inevitably.

key_terms.اسْتَخَارَ: To seek Allah's choice or guidance in a matter

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Allah to choose good for a person who performs Istikhara?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights that *Istikhara* is not merely a ritual for decision-making but a test of *Rida* (contentment) with the Divine Decree (*Hakam*). It emphasizes that true reliance on Allah involves accepting His choice with satisfaction, ensuring that the outcome aligns with one's ultimate spiritual good.

en.hubeali: H 14778 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Usman Bin Isa, from haroun Bin Kharjat, who has said: Abu Abdullahasws has said:
‘The one who leaves the choice to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and is happy with whatsoever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Chooses for him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will inevitably Choose good for him’.
en.sarwar: 331. A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Usman Bin Isa, from haroun Bin Kharjat, who has said: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said:
‘The one who leaves the choice to Allah (azwj) and is happy with whatsoever Allah (azwj) Chooses for him, Allah (azwj) will inevitably Choose good for him’.
